Jude 1.summary: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, writes to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, called, with mercy, peace, and love multiplied (Jude 1:1–2). When he gave all diligence to write of the common salvation, it was needful to exhort them to earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints, because certain men crept in unawares, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness and denying the only Lord God and our Lord Jesus Christ (Jude 1:3–4). He puts them in remembrance that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not, and that the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness, and Sodom and Gomorrha and the cities about them are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire (Jude 1:5–7). These dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities, yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said The Lord rebuke thee (Jude 1:8–10). They have gone in the way of Cain, ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core, and they are spots in the feasts of charity, clouds without water, trees whose fruit withereth, raging waves of the sea, and wandering stars (Jude 1:11–13). Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied that the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment upon all, and these are murmurers and complainers, walking after their own lusts (Jude 1:14–16). The beloved are to remember the words of the apostles, who told them there should be mockers in the last time, who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit (Jude 1:17–19). They are to build up themselves on their most holy faith, pray in the Holy Ghost, keep themselves in the love of God, look for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life, have compassion of some, and save others with fear, pulling them out of the fire (Jude 1:20–23). Unto him that is able to keep them from falling and to present them faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, to the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever (Jude 1:24–25).
Jude 1.whereWeAre: Jude follows 3 John and is the last of the general letters before Revelation. Jude urges believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered unto the saints, gives examples of judgment on the ungodly, and closes with a call to keep themselves in the love of God and praise to him who is able to keep them from falling (1:1-25). Revelation follows.

keyFigures.name: Jude
keyFigures.role: The servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, who exhorts them to earnestly contend for the faith (1:1,3).

keyFigures.name: The sanctified and called
keyFigures.role: Preserved in Jesus Christ, told to build up themselves, pray in the Holy Ghost, and keep themselves in the love of God (1:1,20-21).

keyFigures.name: The ungodly men crept in unawares
keyFigures.role: Turn the grace of God into lasciviousness, deny the only Lord God, defile the flesh, and walk after their own lusts (1:4,8,16).

keyFigures.name: Michael the archangel
keyFigures.role: Durst not bring a railing accusation against the devil but said The Lord rebuke thee (1:9).

keyFigures.name: Enoch
keyFigures.role: The seventh from Adam, who prophesied that the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints (1:14-15).

keyFigures.name: The Lord
keyFigures.role: Destroyed them that believed not, reserves the angels in chains, and is able to keep them from falling (1:5-6,24).

keyThemes.explanation: Jude exhorts them to earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints, because ungodly men crept in unawares (1:3-4).

keyThemes.theme: Grace is not a license for immorality
keyThemes.explanation: The ungodly turn the grace of our God into lasciviousness and deny the only Lord God and our Lord Jesus Christ (1:4).
The Lord destroyed those who believed not, kept the angels in chains, and made Sodom and Gomorrha an example of the vengeance of eternal fire (1:5-16).
The beloved are to keep themselves in the love of God, and he is able to keep them from falling (1:20-21,24-25).
They are to have compassion of some, making a difference, and save others with fear, pulling them out of the fire (1:22-23).
